props.summary: Multipurpose state byte. FUN 0004f050 maintains bit 5 as the 4500/5000 RPM gate for vehicle-speed fuel cut; FUN 0004f19c uses bit 7 as its speed-entry arming state. FUN 000bd20a writes bit 1 as the intake idle-source condition: set only with intake electrical enable ffff248b bit 1, CLSD THL POS copy ffff2458 bit 5, vehicle-speed byte ffff110e at most ROM8[0000871d]=2, engine speed of 1500 RPM (1400 RPM to hold), the raw coolant, oil, intake-air, and normalized BFS flags, and a set of inhibit bits and stored-fault records clear, and held clear after the first activation while re-arm countdown ffff2527 is nonzero; a set bit also sets intake operating bit ffff246b bit 6; while it is set, FUN 000bdc66 conditions idle source byte ffff1553 into intake target ffff2326 in place of the coolant-selected map byte. FUN 000bfe88 maintains bit 3 as the exhaust-VTC demand flag: set while coolant-selected target ffff1c90, plus hysteresis ROM8[000086f4] once set, reaches ROM8[00008dcb]+128, and cleared otherwise. A set bit 3 ORs bits 0 and 1 into bank-enable byte ffff1246. Coordinator 00090a84 maintains bit 4 through comparator 000259d0 as engine-speed byte ffff11b2 at most ROM8[00008dca]=0 with release offset 16, the stopped-engine condition of the exhaust cam reference learning and of FUN 00090bd2.
note: Bit5 gates active stateffff24a6.bit0. Bit7 records entry arming: a new arm loads ROM8[00008caf], an existing arm retains its unsigned counter, and active speed at release or above preserves this bit even with the RPM gate. Other bit roles retain their independent evidence.

props.summary: Previous-cycle coarse vehicle-speed byte. Scheduler 00020dfe copies ffff118e here. FUN 00050018 uses stock boundary 4 to separate the low-speed three-class DFCO restore classifier from moving branches; FUN 0004f324 requires zero before the stationary rev-limiter state can advance. P0128 model functions also use boundaries 2 and shifted coordinates.
note: Exact firmware decodes CAN 0x280 bytes 4 and 5, filters the value through ffff113c/ffff115e, and FUN 0003a254 divides it by 20 into ffff118e. Homologous Z34 CAN data identifies this field as vehicle speed; the resulting byte uses approximately 2 km/h per count. The DFCO boundary is therefore approximately 8 km/h, while the physical scale remains a hardware-validation item.

props.title: Coarse vehicle-speed fuel-cut state with RPM gate
props.summary: Bounded coarse vehicle-speed cut state. Inactive raw speed at activation or above arms control bit7 and loads the zero delay only on a new arm; an existing nonzero counter waits. Counter zero with control bit5 clear sets state bit0. Active speed at release or above holds unless control bit5 gates it; below release clears state bit0 and arm. Complete other state/control bits, unrelated RAM, natural CPU/frame state and bound ROM retain their declared values. This invocation does not decrement the counter.
note: The candidate speed conversion is approximately 186/182 km/h and requires hardware validation.

props.note: Bit5 set clears statebit0 even while active; all other control bits retain their independently owned roles.

Bit7 clear at an inactive activation loads the stock delay and sets the arm; a held arm retains the counter. At active speed at release or above, the incoming arm remains even when bit5 gates active state.
Raw byte comparisons admit activation equality93 and retain active release equality91; unsigned byte ordering includes128..255. Physical speed conversion is outside this invocation.
Incoming bit0 selects release or activation comparison; every other state bit is preserved.

props.summary: Vehicle-speed fuel-cut state byte. Natural 0004f19c preserves all bits other than bit0. Inclusive activation is raw93, exclusive release raw91. A newly armed stock zero delay permits immediate activation with the RPM gate clear; an already armed nonzero counter waits. An active RPM gate clears bit0 independently of the arm. Physical conversion and the global coordinator retain separate evidence.
note: Candidate conversion places the entry/release thresholds near 186/182 km/h; hardware validation remains required.

1.note: With snapshot ffff2458.bit5 of upstream DFCO mode bit ffff2459.bit5 clear, 0004fbe2 requests no cut and 00050018 returns inhibit class 1.

2.note: On a rising edge (previous ffff245a.bit5 clear, coarse speed >= 4) 0004fbe2 requests cut when ffff11b3 > Entry threshold, x*25 RPM by coolant.

3.note: While the mode bit is held, 0004fbe2 compares ffff11b3 with the Hold threshold, x*25 RPM by coolant; a higher threshold needs more RPM to cut.

4.note: Cut request is 1 only while RPM/25 ffff11b3 is strictly above the selected threshold; 00050018 compares the same byte with the restore thresholds.

5.note: 00050018 interpolates Full Restore 0x12818 by coolant into lower threshold ffff16aa, RPM/25, after runtime floors and offsets.

6.note: 00050018 interpolates Intermediate Restore 0x1298C by coolant into upper threshold ffff1778, RPM/25, after runtime floors and offsets.

7.note: The class of RPM-drop byte ffff106a at 0x11CB5 = [4, 8, 12] selects restore floor 0x1299C = [36, 48, 54, 62] RPM/25 (900..1550 RPM).

8.note: ffff11b3 <= ffff16aa returns full-restore class 3; entry from idle needs class 0, so a higher threshold vetoes DFCO up to a higher RPM.

9.note: Below coarse speed 4, ffff16aa < ffff11b3 <= ffff1778 returns intermediate class 2; stock moving branches do not compare ffff1778.

10.note: 000503e0 steps idle, entry delays, full cut, and exit delay; table 0x2371C gives D = 00, 00, 15, 3F, 15 and 0004ed88 forms P = G | D | C.

13.note: Active main cut bit ffff2497.bit2 is one of the 15 global Booleans, so 0004ed88 sets G = 0x3F for all six channels.

14.note: Readiness bit 4 sets when accumulator ffff16a6 reaches ROM16[0x911C] = 381; any failed entry gate clears ffff16a6 and bits 3..5.

15.note: Each 100-count expiry adds lookup(0x124D2 at clamp((ffff11bc - 160) / 2, 0, 255)) - 128 to ffff16a6; stock step 0 at <= 2000 RPM, 127 at the limiter.

16.note: With readiness set and coarse speed ffff110e = 0, RPM/50 ffff11ae >= ROM8[0x85D9] = 36 (1800 RPM) sets bit 5; it clears below 30 (1500 RPM).

17.note: Stationary cut bit ffff247f.bit5 enters the same global Boolean group and becomes a full 0x3F mask.

19.note: Active vehicle-speed cut bit ffff24a6.bit0 is a global Boolean and makes G = 0x3F.

20.note: P1217: raw coolant ffff1071 >= ROM8[0x8D15] = 190 sets, >= 180 retains; bit 5 also needs 1900/1700 RPM hysteresis and ffff2458.bit5 clear.

21.note: Overtemperature fuel-inhibit bit ffff41f2.bit5 is a global Boolean and makes G = 0x3F.

22.note: While service 0x30 IOLID 0x0C is active, 00050a34 returns Power Balance mask ffff2b2c in place of P; the ETC-fault mask A is ORed after it.
